$schema_note: Product-capability catalog for Service Buddy. Keys off plain-language founder phrases, not AWS service names. See catalog/README.md for the fallback rule.
verified_against: floci/floci server v2.0.1, 2026-09-05, via `aws --endpoint-url=http://localhost:4566` with dummy test/test credentials

phrases: users can sign up and log in
capabilities.founder_description: Lets people create an account and log in securely.

steps: create-user-pool-client (no secret, for a web/mobile app)
provision.cli: POOL=$(aws cognito-idp create-user-pool --pool-name <name> --query UserPool.Id --output text) && aws cognito-idp create-user-pool-client --user-pool-id "$POOL" --client-name <name>-app --explicit-auth-flows ALLOW_USER_PASSWORD_AUTH ALLOW_REFRESH_TOKEN_AUTH > /dev/null && echo "$POOL"

verify.cli: CID=$(aws cognito-idp list-user-pool-clients --user-pool-id <userPoolId> --query 'UserPoolClients[0].ClientId' --output text) && U="gatecheck-$(date +%s%N)@example.com" && aws cognito-idp sign-up --client-id "$CID" --username "$U" --password 'GateCheck123!' > /dev/null && aws cognito-idp admin-confirm-sign-up --user-pool-id <userPoolId> --username "$U" > /dev/null && aws cognito-idp initiate-auth --client-id "$CID" --auth-flow USER_PASSWORD_AUTH --auth-parameters USERNAME="$U",PASSWORD='GateCheck123!' > /dev/null && aws cognito-idp admin-delete-user --user-pool-id <userPoolId> --username "$U"
verify.success_criteria: a real sign-up, confirm, login, and cleanup delete all succeed -- not just that the pool exists
verify.founder_proof: created a test account, signed in as them, then deleted it
verify.hardened_note: Round-trips a real sign-up and login, not just a pool lookup: a pool can exist while sign-in is misconfigured. Discovers the pool's client via list-user-pool-clients, since the plan only carries userPoolId, not clientId.

capabilities.cloud_equivalent_note: Same Cognito User Pool concept in real AWS — no redesign needed to retarget.

capabilities.founder_description: Lets people upload and store files (like photos), and get them back later.

steps: create bucket named after the app, e.g. <app-slug>-uploads

verify.cli: K=__gate_check__/$(date +%s%N); echo gate-check-$K > /tmp/__gate_check__.txt && aws s3 cp /tmp/__gate_check__.txt s3://<bucketName>/$K && aws s3 cp s3://<bucketName>/$K /tmp/__gate_check_out__.txt && cmp -s /tmp/__gate_check__.txt /tmp/__gate_check_out__.txt && aws s3 rm s3://<bucketName>/$K
verify.success_criteria: a real write, read-back with matching content, and cleanup delete all succeed -- not just that the bucket exists
verify.founder_proof: stored a test file, read it back unchanged, then removed it
verify.hardened_note: Round-trips a write, read-back, and delete, not just a list: a bucket can be listable while every write or delete in it is blocked (e.g. by S3 Object Lock).

capabilities.cloud_equivalent_note: Same S3 bucket concept in real AWS.

capabilities.founder_description: A place to save and look up structured information, like user profiles or orders.

steps: create-table with a partition key inferred from the request, e.g. 'id'
provision.cli: aws dynamodb create-table --table-name <name> --attribute-definitions AttributeName=id,AttributeType=S --key-schema AttributeName=id,KeyType=HASH --billing-mode PAY_PER_REQUEST > /dev/null && aws dynamodb wait table-exists --table-name <name> && echo <name>

verify.cli: K="gatecheck-$(date +%s%N)" && aws dynamodb put-item --table-name <tableName> --item "{\"id\":{\"S\":\"$K\"}}" > /dev/null && aws dynamodb get-item --table-name <tableName> --key "{\"id\":{\"S\":\"$K\"}}" | grep -q "$K" && aws dynamodb delete-item --table-name <tableName> --key "{\"id\":{\"S\":\"$K\"}}"
verify.success_criteria: a real save, look-up with matching content, and cleanup delete all succeed -- not just that the table exists
verify.founder_proof: saved a test record, looked it back up, then removed it
verify.hardened_note: Round-trips a real save, look-up, and delete, not just a describe: a table can exist while reads or writes against it fail.

capabilities.cloud_equivalent_note: Same DynamoDB table concept in real AWS.

phrases: do something automatically when a file is uploaded
process something without the user waiting
capabilities.founder_description: Runs a small piece of work in the background (like resizing a photo) without making the user wait.

steps: create-function from a small starter handler
wire an S3 event notification (ObjectCreated) to invoke it
provision.cli: D=$(mktemp -d) && printf "def handler(event, context):\n    return {\"ok\": True}\n" > "$D/index.py" && python3 -c "import sys,zipfile; z=zipfile.ZipFile(sys.argv[1],\"w\"); z.write(sys.argv[2],\"index.py\"); z.close()" "$D/fn.zip" "$D/index.py" && aws lambda create-function --function-name <name> --runtime python3.12 --handler index.handler --role arn:aws:iam::000000000000:role/service-buddy-exec --zip-file "fileb://$D/fn.zip" > /dev/null && aws lambda wait function-active-v2 --function-name <name> && echo <name>

verify.cli: aws lambda invoke --function-name <functionName> --payload '{}' --cli-binary-format raw-in-base64-out /tmp/__gate_lambda_out__.json > /tmp/__gate_lambda_meta__.json && ! grep -q FunctionError /tmp/__gate_lambda_meta__.json
verify.success_criteria: a real invoke with test input completes without a function error -- not just that the function is registered
verify.founder_proof: ran it once with test input and it finished successfully
verify.hardened_note: Invokes the function with test input, not just a registration check: a function can be registered and still fail on every run.

capabilities.cloud_equivalent_note: Same Lambda + S3 event-notification pattern in real AWS.

capabilities.founder_description: Sends an email to a user, like a confirmation or welcome message.

provision.cli: aws ses verify-email-identity --email-address noreply@<name>.example.com && echo noreply@<name>.example.com

verify.cli: FROM=$(aws ses list-identities --query 'Identities[0]' --output text) && aws ses send-email --from "$FROM" --destination "ToAddresses=test@example.com" --message "Subject={Data=Verification check},Body={Text={Data=test}}"
verify.success_criteria: a real test email actually sends -- not just that a sender identity is registered. Discovers the real registered identity rather than assuming resource_name is the email address (resource_name is an internal label, not necessarily an address).
verify.founder_proof: sent a test email and confirmed it went out
verify.hardened_note: Sends a real test email, not just an identity lookup: a sender can be registered and still unable to send.

capabilities.cloud_equivalent_note: Same SES identity concept in real AWS.

capabilities.founder_description: Runs something automatically on a schedule, like a weekly digest email.

steps: create-schedule targeting an existing Lambda function
provision.cli: Q=$(aws sqs create-queue --queue-name <name>-target --query QueueUrl --output text) && T=$(aws sqs get-queue-attributes --queue-url "$Q" --attribute-names QueueArn --query Attributes.QueueArn --output text) && aws scheduler create-schedule --name <name> --schedule-expression 'rate(1 day)' --flexible-time-window Mode=OFF --target "Arn=$T,RoleArn=arn:aws:iam::000000000000:role/service-buddy-exec" > /dev/null && echo <name>

verify.founder_proof: checked that the schedule is set and active

capabilities.cloud_equivalent_note: Same EventBridge Scheduler concept in real AWS.

phrases: a workflow that runs step by step
an onboarding flow with several steps
capabilities.founder_description: Runs a multi-step process in order -- like checking a signup, sending a welcome email, then logging the result.

steps: create-state-machine from a small starter definition (a linear chain of steps)

verify.cli: EXEC=$(aws stepfunctions start-execution --state-machine-arn <stateMachineArn> --input '{}' --query executionArn --output text) && for i in $(seq 1 10); do STATUS=$(aws stepfunctions describe-execution --execution-arn "$EXEC" --query status --output text); [ "$STATUS" != "RUNNING" ] && break; sleep 1; done && [ "$STATUS" = "SUCCEEDED" ]
verify.success_criteria: a real execution with test input actually completes (SUCCEEDED) within the poll window, not just that the state machine is registered
verify.founder_proof: ran the whole process once end-to-end and every step finished

capabilities.cloud_equivalent_note: Same Step Functions state machine concept in real AWS -- no redesign needed to retarget.
